content.title: The Masters 2019: Tiger Woods' Fifth Green Jacket Caps The Greatest Comeback In Golf History
content.text: AUGUSTA, GEORGIA - APRIL 14: (Sequence frame 6 of 12) Tiger Woods of the United States celebrates after making his putt on the 18th green to win the Masters at Augusta National Golf Club on April 14, 2019 in Augusta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The once unbeatable golfer, who the majority of players in the field at the Masters grew up watching on television, proved he’s no washed-up blast from the past. The book on his era isn't over yet. Tiger Woods is not done winning majors. Woods delivered the goods Sunday topping a leaderboard filled with young guns like Xander Schauffele and Brooks Koepka (both of whom he has almost a couple decades on) to seal the deal on his fifth green jacket and fifteenth major championship. This was one for the ages, reminiscent of Ben Hogan’s return to glory at the 1950 U.S. Open. Hogan had been the victim of a head-on collision with a Greyhound bus and barely made it out of his Cadillac in one piece. Sixteen months later he went on to win a major at Merion. Hogan had to soak and bandage his legs before every round to keep the swelling down caused by that near fatal accident. It’s an incredible story and integral to the Hogan legacy. Now, so is the build-up to Tiger’s fifth green jacket. The injury plagued 43-year old’s body has been subjected to a series of major back surgeries over the years culminating in a spinal fusion to connect his L5 and S1 vertebrae. While healthier than he’s been in years, Woods still requires treatment to tune up his body for tournament play. On Sunday at the Masters he had to wake up at 3:45 a.m. to get prepped for his 9:25 a.m. tee time. Anatomy of a Comeback In late 2009 news of his marital affairs began to leak to the tabloids in a steady drip of raunchy and sordid details that were then amplified tenfold by a social media led lynch mob. Suddenly, the top of the heap golfer who previously enjoyed a squeaky-clean image turned into a pariah overnight with a parade of sponsors including Accenture, AT&T, Gatorade, and Gillette opting to part ways with him. In May of 2017 Woods hit rock bottom with a DUI arrest after the golfer was found asleep at the wheel and failed sobriety tests. The resulting bleary-eyed mugshot of Tiger is still a popular meme. In 2018, with his health finally returning, Woods rededicated himself to competitive golf and accrued a bunch of top ten finishes over the course of the season. But skepticism lingered about the legitimacy of Tiger’s comeback until he topped the leaderboard once again winning the 2018 Tour Championship, his 80th career PGA TOUR win. Congratulations, Tiger! To come back and win the Masters after all the highs and lows is a testament to excellence, grit, and determination. — Barack Obama (@BarackObama) April 14, 2019 Following the victory, the conventional wisdom was that Woods’ chances of ever winning a major again still remained somewhat slim as proven by the seven figure losses suffered by sportsbooks following El Tigre’s fifth Masters win. Tiger is now the only player aside from Jack Nicklaus to win Masters tournaments in three different decades. Also, the fourteen year span between this victory and his last Masters triumph in 2005 is the longest gap between victories at Augusta National, eclipsing Gary Player’s long-held mark. Tiger’s dominance in his heyday was so incredible that no fans would’ve guessed back in 2008 when a grimacing Tiger Woods persevered to win the U.S. Open on a Monday playoff, overcoming the pain of a torn anterior cruciate ligament on his knee and stress fractures on his left leg that eleven years later he’d still be on the hunt for a follow-up major victory to get to fifteen—just three shy of Jack’s record. Not to be left out, Tiger’s caddie Joe LaCava earned his second Masters win on the bag. His first came back in 1992 with Freddie Couples.
